taxonomyNote: NatureServe spells the common name 'Smooth Greensnake' and notes some authors placed the species in genus Liochlorophis; Animal Diversity Web uses 'Smooth Green Snake'.
fieldMarks: Slender, bright green above with smooth dorsal scales (15 rows at midbody) and a white or yellowish belly.
Adults usually 30-51 cm, up to about 61 cm; the tail is nearly half of total length.
Young are dull olive-gray to bluish-gray or grayish brown; adults turn blue or gray after death.
Smooth scales separate it from the rough green snake (keeled scales); single nostril scale and smaller size separate it from racers.
behavior: Diurnal; basks on boulders or logs and may hang in low branches; inactive roughly November-March.
Eats small terrestrial invertebrates such as caterpillars, crickets, grasshoppers and spiders.
Can aggregate in hibernacula (groups of 100-150 found in Manitoba and Minnesota) and sometimes uses abandoned ant mounds.
Eggs are laid under rotting wood, underground or under rocks; some individuals cross roads at night during warm rains.
habitat: Grassy, open areas: meadows, grassy marshes, moist fields at forest edges, bogs, stream borders and open moist woodland.
Often near wetlands or open water.
range: Nova Scotia west across southern Canada (Quebec, Ontario, Manitoba) to southeastern Saskatchewan, south through the northeastern and Midwestern US to Virginia, Missouri, Nebraska, New Mexico and Utah; western populations are highly disjunct.

lookalikes.name: Rough green snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Has keeled rather than smooth dorsal scales.

lookalikes.name: Racer
lookalikes.howToTell: Larger; nostril sits between two scales rather than centred in one scale.
